title: Glasgow & the Barrens
summary: Barren County, home of Glasgow, was created on December 20, 1798, from Green and Warren counties and named for the open grasslands called the barrens.
bodyMarkdown:
Barren County, home of Glasgow, takes its name from "the barrens," the open grasslands that early travelers found across south-central Kentucky. The Kentucky legislature created the county on December 20, 1798, carving it from parts of Green and Warren counties. The [Kentucky Historical Society's marker for Barren County](https://history.ky.gov/markers/barren-county-1798) on the Glasgow courthouse lawn records that origin.

## Prairie country

The barrens were [treeless stretches](https://grokipedia.com/page/Barren_County,_Kentucky) covering much of the county's northern third. Early surveyors noted their treeless expanses. Before the county existed, the area belonged to Logan County, the first jurisdiction south of the Green River.

Long hunters reached the region before settlers did. Parties tied to [Henry Skaggs](/stories/henry-skaggs-green-river-long-hunter/) crossed southern Kentucky's hills and prairies in search of game. Permanent farms followed in the late 1790s, many on land grants given to Revolutionary War veterans.

## Choosing a county seat

Glasgow was founded in 1799 to serve as the county seat. [A history of Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasgow,_Kentucky) gives the reasons the site won: a central location, a large spring, and John Gorin's donation of 50 acres for public buildings. Gorin also opened a tavern that year to serve travelers and new settlers.

The town's name is less settled. The name honors the Scottish hometown of the father of William Logan, one of two commissioners who chose the seat. One account [credits trustee John Matthews](https://grokipedia.com/page/Glasgow,_Kentucky), a native of Glasgow, Scotland. Both accounts tie the name to Scotland.

## A town takes shape

Early Glasgow grew slowly. Matthews and John Anderson [were among](https://grokipedia.com/page/Glasgow,_Kentucky) the first to run blacksmith forges, making tools for the settlers. A post office opened in 1803, and the town received its city rights in 1809.

Farm families across the county raised crops and livestock. Mills, cotton gins, sawmills, distilleries and blacksmith shops grew up along local creeks and rivers.

## Through the Civil War

The KHS marker also records Barren County's place in the Civil War. It notes the early stages of Confederate Gen. John Hunt Morgan's 1862 raids and Gen. Braxton Bragg's invasion of Kentucky. Morgan's forces [raided](https://grokipedia.com/page/Glasgow,_Kentucky) Glasgow twice in 1862.

## Kentucky today

Glasgow remains the Barren County seat, and the county marker still stands on the courthouse lawn. A small part of Mammoth Cave National Park lies in the county's northwest, and Barren River Lake, impounded by a dam in neighboring Allen County, reaches into the area.
